text:
maya singh: heads up — noticed intermittent reconnect spikes for tenant=acme around 12:00 UTC, looks correlated to proxy keepalive churn. console shows duplicate session counts :thinking_face:
raj patel: timeline? client or gateway side? any 5xx or 204s?
maya singh: started ~11:58, lasted ~6m. no 5xx, lots of 204 and then resume attempts. sample logs below.
Olga B.: pasted grep from the proxy logs:
```
[2024-03-12T11:58:12Z] proxy: tenant=acme session=abc123 keepalive_miss=1 route=us-east-1
[2024-03-12T11:58:12Z] proxy: tenant=acme session=abc123 proxied_status=204 resume_allowed=false
[2024-03-12T11:58:12Z] client: tenant=acme session=abc123 reconnect start=1
```
raj patel: interesting — proxied_status=204 + resume_allowed=false will cause client to reconnect fresh, which increments billing counters. that explains dup counts.
maya singh: console shows billing spike at the same minute. we need to avoid forcing fresh reconnects where resume is possible.
sre-bot: Alert: streaming-reconnects-high (tenant=acme) — rate 120/min — triggered at 2024-03-12T11:59:00Z
console-bot: snapshot: https://console/internal/dashboards/streams?tenant=acme&ts=2024-03-12T11:58
devex-liz: is this new after the last proxy rollout? we changed the keepalive probe window last week.
Olga B.: rollout note: proxy v2.14 toggled keepalive aggressive GC (ttl=30s -> ttl=15s) last Thu. might be too aggressive for noisy mobile clients.
raj patel: reproduce plan: spin up a test client that stalls on next chunk and see if proxy returns 204 vs 200+resume header. likely bug: proxy GC is zapping session before router marks resume_allowed. race between session-ttl and ack-window.
maya singh: short term workaround: increase sticky lease TTL to 60s for affected routes? will that risk resource leakage?
raj patel: tradeoff but fine for canary. also add a small grace window for resume header emission: when session_gc is imminent, emit resume_allowed=true for 10s.
devex-liz: we should gate this behind a config flag and gradual canary. can update rollout UX to show affected tenants.
Olga B.: another wrinkle — clients with aggressive recon backoff will hammer resume path while routing swap happens, so need backoff tweak. suggestion config: 
```yaml
streaming:
  keepalive_interval: 30s
  session_ttl: 60s
  resume_grace: 10s
  reconnect_backoff:
    initial_ms: 250
    max_ms: 8000
    jitter: true
```
maya singh: that backoff max looks ok. also need console telemetry labels: route_id, proxy_version, resume_allowed boolean so we can pivot in dashboards. right now console groups by tenant only and it's noisy.
console-bot: filed dashboard request #ENG-4287 to add labels and a stacked time series for resume_allowed vs fresh_reconnects. will post screenshot when ready.
raj patel: low-effort patch: change proxy to set "resume_allowed=true" if session.touch_time > now - resume_grace, and ensure response code 200 with header instead of 204 when possible. small PR incoming.
Olga B.: logging snippet when it happens:
```
[2024-03-12T11:58:12Z] proxy.DEBUG preserve_session: session=abc123 touch=2024-03-12T11:58:05 ttl=15s -> decision=GC (emit_resume=false)
[2024-03-12T11:58:12Z] router.INFO route-swap: session=abc123 target=pod-22 fallback=pod-5
[2024-03-12T11:58:12Z] client.INFO reconnect: session=abc123 new_session=def456 billing_increment=1
```
maya singh: can you add a metric emit (resume_allowed: bool) in that code path? then we can create an alert when resume_allowed=false spikes.
raj patel: agreed. also add a small canary rollout: 5% of routes with extended ttl + resume_grace=10s. we should monitor token billing delta.
devex-liz: I'll prepare a console UX note for the rollout — include instructions for ops to toggle per-route and how to revert.
Olga B.: created PR #1042 with the header change + metric. applying to canary namespace now.
maya singh: awesome. tagging @sre-oncall to watch for billing blips. thanks all. :thumbsup:
sre-bot: Annotated runbook: if billing delta > 10% for tenant during canary, rollback and set session_ttl back to 15s.
maya singh: follow-up: can someone add a quick e2e that simulates intermittent chunk stall to catch regressions? low-friction harness would be enough.
raj patel: I'll add a unit+integration test in the router/proxy suite. ETA EOD.
Olga B.: keeping an eye on canary logs, will report back in ~20m.
maya singh: thanks — will update the dashboard ticket when we see initial telemetry.
